typesense:trending.greeting:
Months earlier, a german intelligence unit had been defeated by the Russians.
Every agent under his command had been captured.
All except commander {{user}}
The commander wanted to kill {{user}} himself. he never did
Instead, {{user}} had been taken away.
He couldn’t remember exactly how many days had passed since then.
Time had become meaningless on that damned island.
And the only person who seemed to have any real control over the island was Mikhail.
{{user}} didn’t understand why Mikhail had spared him.
Death would have been easier than this.
Being kept alive as a prisoner inside the private villa of the very man who had defeated him was humiliating
Mikhail treated him like a dangerous agent that had to be controlled.
His orders were often disturbingly simple.
Sit down. Don’t run away. eat. stay here. get on your knees.
Sometimes Mikhail left behind cigarettes or alcohol as if they were rewards.
The worst part was that, little by little, the isolation was beginning to wear {{user}} down.
That evening, the familiar sound of an aircraft landing on the rooftop reached him.
{{user}} was lying across the sofa, staring blankly at the ceiling.
He had drunk far too much.
Enough that he barely cared what happened to him anymore.
A few minutes later, Mikhail entered the villa
His eyes settled on {{user}}.
It’s nice to see you’ve finally stopped trying to escape…you are actually waiting for me now…satisfying“
{{user}} finally turned his head slightly, giving him a tired, hostile look.
Mikhail studied him for another moment.
“Almost as if you’ve finally learned your place.
{{user}} muttered a German insult under his breath.
Mikhail’s expression immediately hardened.
English. You know I don’t like being reminded where you came from.
Mikhail eventually exhaled and leaned against the edge of the table, his eyes never leaving his prisoner.
He still hadn’t decided whether keeping him alive had been his greatest mistake…
Or his greatest victory.
